senses.definition: That which causes wonder; a prodigy; a portent.

quotes.text: The mysteries of this wonderful universe rise more palpable upon the departing spirit, so soon to mingle with their marvels.
quotes.reference: 1834, L[etitia] E[lizabeth] L[andon], chapter XXIV, in Francesca Carrara. […], volume II, London: Richard Bentley, […], (successor to Henry Colburn), →OCLC, page 261:

quotes.text: He found ways to film fiery, elaborate car-wrecks, keeping everything visually clear and beautiful without killing or even seriously injuring anyone. On a sheer technical level, the movie is a marvel.
quotes.reference: 2017 December 1, Tom Breihan, “Mad Max: Fury Road might already be the best action movie ever made”, in The Onion AV Club:

quotes.text: No maruel though you bite so sharp at reasons,

senses.definition: (intransitive) To become filled with wonderment or admiration; to be amazed at something.

quotes.text: Marueile not, my brethren, if the world hate you.
quotes.reference: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London: […] Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, 1 John 3:13, column 1:

quotes.text: Men marvel at the works of man / And with unstinted praises sing / The greatness of some worldly thing / Encompassed during one life's span;
quotes.reference: 1923, Robert Louis Stevenson, “Men marvel at the works of man”, in The Complete Poems of Robert Louis Stevenson, New York: Charles Scribner's Sons, page 466:

quotes.text: The ads show tourists hiking with a selfie stick, (“Very nice!”), drinking fermented horse milk (“Mm, that’s actually very nice!”), marvelling at the architecture (“Wow, very nice!”) and posing for a photograph with Kazakhs in traditional dress (“That’s very nice!”).
quotes.reference: 2020 October 27, Helen Sullivan, “'Very nice!': Kazakhstan adopts Borat's catchphrase in new tourism campaign”, in The Guardian, →ISSN:

quotes.text: If Cleopatra or Elizabeth I were to time-travel to the present day, they would marvel at a world we take for granted, with its vaccines and antibiotics, and a flushing toilet and fridge in every home.
quotes.reference: 2021 June 25, Richard Fisher, “Generational amnesia: The memory loss that harms the planet”, in BBC News:

quotes.text: I maruell that her Grace did leaue it out.

quotes.text: I maruell why I answer'd not againe,
